descriptionChirho: Fire in both literal and eschatological senses, encompassing the physical phenomenon of combustion as well as divine judgment by fire. All three clusters represent the same core meaning — fire — differing only in case usage (nominative/accusative/genitive/dative) and the prepositions governing them. Multilingual evidence is perfectly uniform: Spanish 'fuego' (with prepositional variants 'de fuego,' 'con fuego,' 'para fuego'), Hindi 'आग' (with postpositions '-की,' '-से,' '-में,' '-के लिए'), Arabic 'نارٍ' / 'بِنَارٍ' / 'لِلنّارِ' (fire / with fire / for fire), Korean '불' / '불에' / '불의' (fire / in fire / of fire), Swahili 'moto' / 'kwa moto' (fire / by fire). No semantic distinction exists across these clusters.
